The Gutenberg Galaxy catapulted Marshall McLuhan to fame as a media theorist and, in time, a new media prognosticator. Fifty years after its initial publication, this landmark text is more significant than ever before.

...

The Gutenberg Galaxy foresaw the networked, compressed ‘global village’ that would emerge in the late-twentieth and twenty-first centuries — despite having been written when black-and-white television was ubiquitous.
This new edition of The Gutenberg Galaxy celebrates both the centennial of McLuhan’s birth and the fifty-year anniversary of the book’s publication.

_**The Gutenberg Galaxy: The Making of Typographic Man**_ is a 1962 book by [Marshall McLuhan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/

...

McLuhan described it as one which "develops a [mosaic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mosaic "Mosaic") or field approach to its problems". [[ 10 ]]() The mosaic image to be constructed from data and quotations would then reveal "causal operations in history". [[ 11 ]]()

The book consists of five parts:

* Prologue
* The Gutenberg Galaxy
* The Galaxy Reconfigured
* Bibliographic Index
* Index of Chapter Glosses

The main body of the book, "The Gutenberg Galaxy", consists of 107 short "chapters".

Apparently, McLuhan also had some ideas about how to browse a book. _Marshall McLuhan, the guru of The Gutenberg Galaxy_ (1962), recommends that the browser turn to page 69 of any book and read it.
